newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna cancels launch of most CECE derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Vienna cancels launch of most CECE derivatives.

text.p: Austria's OeTOB futures and options exchange said on Wednesday it was delaying the launch of derivatives trade on most of its Central European Clearing House and Exchange products due to a shortage of market makers.
In a statement, OeTOB said only futures and options trade on its Hungarian Traded Index would go ahead as planned on as planned on March 20.
The exchange would not offer derivatives, however, on the Polish Traded Index, Czech Traded Index and the Central European Clearing House and Exchange (CECE) Index.
Earlier this month, OeTOB said there was plenty of market interest for the new instruments and forecast average daily turnover would reach 2,000 contracts by the end of the year.
Bank fuer Arbeit und Wirtschaft AG (BAWAG), Investmentbank Austria and Creditanstalt Investment Bank will act as market makers for the Hungarian Traded Index.
OeTOB said it still hoped derivatives trade on the Czech Traded Index could begin in the next few months.
